summary.core_contribution: The paper automatically builds an approximate workflow model and adaptive quantitative constraints from user-space and kernel execution traces, reducing manual model construction for real-time and multicore diagnosis.
summary.problem: Manual model and constraint construction for concurrent real-time applications requires substantial system knowledge and effort, even though low-overhead tracing provides the evidence needed for verification.
summary.method: The method organizes trace events per thread, groups similar sequences with longest-common-subsequence matching using strict or flexible key-value matching, removes unneeded repetitions, builds a state model, and infers adaptive constraint operators and values from runtime timing distributions. The model is presented for user checking and correction; LTTng is explicitly used in the cyclictest case.
summary.findings: The generated model detects the JACK2 xrun, the cyclictest outlier, and the in-kernel wakelock priority inversion. For cyclictest, a manually set 3-ms deadline is inferred as about 2.685 ms. In the reported evaluation, model construction is dominant - about 7 minutes for full cyclictest - while traces range from 321 UST and 419,164 kernel events for JACK2 to 41,677 UST and 208,489 kernel events for cyclictest and 42 UST and 194,997 kernel events for wakelock.
summary.limitations: Generated models can contain extra constraints and still need user correction. The evaluation emphasizes common real-time cases with relatively simple loops and does not establish performance across more complex modeling requirements.
summary.future_work: Build and detect models on the fly, compatible with LTTng flight-recorder mode.
